paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption: Inter-annotator agreement compared to sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity values.
model_annotation: This figure consists of two side-by-side bar charts illustrating inter-annotator agreement (measured by Fleiss Kappa) in relation to sample-level ambiguity metrics. The left chart has the horizontal axis labeled "Ambiguity Std" with four categories: 0.0, 0.47, 0.82, and 0.94, and the vertical axis labeled "Fleiss Kappa" with a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to approximately 0.9, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The bars are all dark blue (teal) in color. The tallest bar corresponds to Ambiguity Std of 0.0 with a value of 0.88, followed by 0.47 with a value of 0.46, then 0.94 with a value of 0.24, and the shortest bar at 0.82 with a value of 0.03. Each bar is annotated with its exact value above it. The right chart has the horizontal axis labeled "Max Ambiguity" with three categories: 1, 2, and 3, and the vertical axis labeled "Fleiss Kappa" with the same linear scale ranging from 0.0 to approximately 0.9 with tick marks at 0.2 intervals. The bars are the same dark blue (teal) color. The tallest bar corresponds to Max Ambiguity of 1 with a value of 0.89, followed by 2 with a value of 0.46, and the shortest bar at 3 with a value of 0.23. Each bar is also annotated with its exact value. In both charts, the bars appear ordered by their category labels from left to right, and the Fleiss Kappa values generally decrease as the ambiguity metric increases, though no explicit sorting by value is indicated.
